title: openOODA MCP Server
content:
## MCP_SETUP — Setup

The openOODA MCP (Model Context Protocol) server is a pure-.`oo` self-hosted MCP server. It speaks MCP protocol version `2024-11-05` over stdio (JSON-RPC 2.0 framed) and provides `tools/list`, `tools/call`, `resources/list`, `resources/read`, `prompts/list`, `prompts/get`, and a `ping` health probe.

The server is one of seven openOODA subsystems. It is a transport-only adapter: it parses JSON-RPC envelopes, runs an OODA dispatch loop, and emits framed responses. All semantic logic lives in the engine sub-modules under `engine/`.

### Installation

The MCP server ships as part of the `mcp` package. Install the `ooda` toolchain, then add the `mcp` package to your project:

```sh
# 1. install the ooda toolchain (one-time)
oodaup install ooda@2.10.0

# 2. add the mcp package to your project
oodaup add mcp@0.5.0

# 3. verify the install
ooda mcp --help
```

The mcp package declares its compatibility range in `VERSION`:

```
mcp=0.5.0
ooda=2.10.0
ooda_max=2.99.0
oodac=2.10.0
std=2.10.0
api_surface=7
```

The mcp package refuses to run if the installed ooda toolchain is outside the declared range.

### Environment variables

The server reads one environment variable:

| Name | Purpose | Default |
|------|---------|---------|
| `OODACODEX` | Override the path to the orientation codex (LLMS.oot) | repo-relative path |

The codex override is resolved under `&EnvCap`. No other environment variables are read.

### Launching the server

The server binary has two subcommands: `mcp` (run the server) and `mcp-merge` (inject the ooda entry into an agent-tool JSON config).

Run the server in stdio mode (the editor case):

```sh
ooda mcp                # equivalent to: ooda mcp --stdio
ooda mcp --stdio        # explicit stdio flag
```

Run the server in one-shot file mode (a single batch read from a file, then exit):

```sh
ooda mcp --file path/to/request.txt
```

Run the server over a Unix socket:

```sh
ooda mcp --socket /tmp/ooda-mcp.sock
```

Inject the openOODA entry into an MCP client config (idempotent):

```sh
ooda mcp-merge ~/.config/openooda/agent-config.json
```

Exit codes for `mcp-merge`: `0` = no-op (already present), `1` = written, `2` = error.

### Transport

The server uses one of three transports, selected at launch:

1. **stdio** (default). The server reads the full stdin chunk, processes it, and writes framed responses to stdout. This is the standard MCP transport for editor integrations.
2. **file**. The server reads one request from the given file path under `&FsReadCap`, processes it, and exits. Use this for batch jobs and CI smoke tests.
3. **socket**. The server binds a Unix-domain socket under `&BindCap` and accepts connections.

All three transports use the same JSON-RPC 2.0 framing.

### JSON-RPC 2.0 framing

The server uses LSP-style Content-Length framing on stdio. Each message is one HTTP-style header followed by a JSON body:

```
Content-Length: 123\r\n
\r\n
{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":1,"method":"initialize","params":{...}}
```

The header is mandatory. Raw JSON objects without the Content-Length header are also accepted by the file transport, but stdio clients should always emit the header.

### MCP vs LSP

The openOODA polyrepo ships both an MCP server and an LSP server. The two share framing but differ in semantics:

| | MCP (this server) | LSP |
|---|---|---|
| Purpose | Tool use for AI agents | Editor-state for IDEs |
| Caller | LLM agent | Code editor |
| Methods | `tools/list`, `tools/call`, `resources/*`, `prompts/*` | `textDocument/*`, `workspace/*`, `completion`, `hover` |
| State | Per-request (session) | Long-lived (open documents) |
| Framing | JSON-RPC 2.0 + Content-Length | JSON-RPC 2.0 + Content-Length |
| Dispatch | OODA: Orient → Decide → Act | LSP: server state machine |
| Capabilities | 14 cap tokens | None |

MCP is request-response for tool use. LSP is editor-state-driven.

### Capabilities (method summary)

| Method | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `initialize` | Lifecycle start, server capabilities |
| `notifications/initialized` | Client ack (notification, no response) |
| `tools/list` | Enumerate the 23 typed tools |
| `tools/call` | Dispatch to a single tool, wrap the result |
| `resources/list` | Enumerate the 8 knowledge resources |
| `resources/read` | Read a specific resource |
| `prompts/list` | Enumerate the 1 prompt template |
| `prompts/get` | Read a prompt template by name |
| `ping` | Heartbeat (returns 7 server-wide health fields) |
| `shutdown` | Graceful shutdown |
| `exit` | Terminate the server |
| `roots/list` | Read the client-declared root URIs |
| `sampling/createMessage` | Refused (server does not sample) |
| `notifications/cancelled` | Mark a request as cancelled |
| `notifications/roots/list_changed` | Client added a new root URI |
| `notifications/progress` | Server-to-client progress frames |

## TOOLS — Tool Catalog

The MCP server exposes **23 typed tools** under `tools/call`. Each tool has a name, a one-line description, an input schema (JSON Schema fragment), and a `requiresCap` bitmask. Tools that read files need `FsReadCap`; tools that write need `FsWriteCap`. A `requiresCap` of `0` means the tool is callable with the default session cap.

All tool results are wrapped in the standard MCP content envelope:

```json
{"content":[{"type":"text","text":"<json-string-payload>"}]}
```

The payload is a JSON string. Clients parse the inner `text` field to recover the typed result.

### The 23 Tools

| # | Name | Tier | Input | Description |
|---|------|------|-------|-------------|
| 1 | `get_capability_graph` | 0 | `{}` | Return the typed sovereign capability graph |
| 2 | `get_orientation` | 0 | `{}` | Return the textual orientation codex |
| 3 | `read_board` | 0 | `{"name":string}` | Read one canonical process board |
| 4 | `refresh_dynamic_graph` | 0 | `{}` | Reload the dynamic graph under FsWriteCap |
| 5 | `get_audit_log` | 0 | `{"tail":int}` | Return the last N audit-log entries |
| 6 | `get_board_index` | 1 | `{}` | List all 13 canonical process boards |
| 7 | `summarize_board` | 1 | `{"name":string,"max_chars":int}` | Read + truncate one board (FsReadCap) |
| 8 | `compress_orient` | 1 | `{"max_chars":int}` | Truncate the orientation codex |
| 9 | `get_context_budget` | 1 | `{}` | Session bytes/seq/caps/audit snapshot |
| 10 | `estimate_chars` | 1 | `{"text":string}` | Char count proxy for token count |
| 11 | `get_ooda_phase` | 2 | `{}` | Current OODA phase (idle/orient/decide/act) |
| 12 | `get_decision_journal` | 2 | `{"n":int}` | Last N substantive decisions |
| 13 | `get_redteam_realtime` | 2 | `{}` | Live fire of all 8 redteam gates |
| 14 | `get_session_diagnostics` | 2 | `{}` | Comprehensive session health snapshot |
| 15 | `get_format_constraints` | 3 | `{}` | Return FORMAT.oot rules as JSON |
| 16 | `validate_codex_format` | 3 | `{"text":string}` | Check a codex text against FORMAT.oot |
| 17 | `get_northstar` | 4 | `{}` | Read the NORTHSTAR board |
| 18 | `get_security_threat_model` | 4 | `{}` | Read SECURITY (threat models) |
| 19 | `get_redteam_methodology` | 4 | `{}` | Read REDTEAM (8D adversarial matrix) |
| 20 | `get_workflow_protocol` | 4 | `{}` | Read WORKFLOW (branching, merge, release) |
| 21 | `get_em_swarm` | 4 | `{}` | Read STRUCTURE_EM (E-M topology) |
| 22 | `get_milestone_status` | 4 | `{}` | Read ROADMAP + SHIPPED merged |
| 23 | `audit_compact` | 4 | `{"keep_last_n":int}` | Drop all but the last N audit entries |

### Tier 0 — Core (5 tools)

The five original tools. All read from the loaded McpGraph substrate.

**`get_capability_graph`** — Input: `{}`. Output: JSON for the typed 14-cap / 13-board / 8-gate graph. `requiresCap: 0`

**`get_orientation`** — Input: `{}`. Output: the textual orientation codex (LLMS.oot). `requiresCap: 0`

**`read_board`** — Input: `{"name":string}` (required). Output: the board's text wrapped in `ooda://orientation/board/<name>` resource envelope. `requiresCap: FsReadCap`

**`refresh_dynamic_graph`** — Input: `{}`. Output: refresh started; fold runs on session close under FsWriteCap. `requiresCap: FsWriteCap`

**`get_audit_log`** — Input: `{"tail":int}` (optional, default 10). Output: the last N entries of the per-session hash-chained audit log. `requiresCap: 0`

### Tier 1 — Token economy (5 tools)

Reduce context-window cost.

**`get_board_index`** — Input: `{}`. Output: array of all 13 boards with name, path, priority, and summary char count. `requiresCap: 0`

**`summarize_board`** — Input: `{"name":string, "max_chars":int}` (both optional, default `max_chars=2000`). Output: the board text truncated to `max_chars`. `requiresCap: FsReadCap`

**`compress_orient`** — Input: `{"max_chars":int}` (optional, default 2000). Output: the orientation codex truncated to `max_chars`. `requiresCap: 0`

**`get_context_budget`** — Input: `{}`. Output: session bytes-in, bytes-out, request seq, caps held, audit count, notification count. `requiresCap: 0`

**`estimate_chars`** — Input: `{"text":string}` (required). Output: the char count of the input text (proxy for token count). `requiresCap: 0`

### Tier 2 — OODA state (4 tools)

Inspect the live OODA loop state.

**`get_ooda_phase`** — Input: `{}`. Output: current phase (one of `idle`, `orient`, `decide`, `act`) and a label. `requiresCap: 0`

**`get_decision_journal`** — Input: `{"n":int}` (optional, default 10). Output: the last N substantive decisions (filtered audit log). `requiresCap: 0`

**`get_redteam_realtime`** — Input: `{}`. Output: live fire of all 8 redteam gates, returned as a JSON array. `requiresCap: 0`

**`get_session_diagnostics`** — Input: `{}`. Output: a comprehensive session health snapshot (phase + tier + caps + counters). `requiresCap: 0`

### Tier 3 — Format (2 tools)

Validate codex format.

**`get_format_constraints`** — Input: `{}`. Output: the FORMAT.oot rules as JSON (4-element header, 5-component WO, 256-line cap). `requiresCap: 0`

**`validate_codex_format`** — Input: `{"text":string}` (required). Output: a list of format violations. `requiresCap: 0`

### Tier 4 — Workspace + audit (7 tools)

Read individual process boards and run audit maintenance.

**`get_northstar`** — Input: `{}`. Output: the NORTHSTAR board (mission and design principles). `requiresCap: FsReadCap`

**`get_security_threat_model`** — Input: `{}`. Output: the SECURITY board (threat models and fail-closed operations). `requiresCap: FsReadCap`

**`get_redteam_methodology`** — Input: `{}`. Output: the REDTEAM board (8D adversarial matrix). `requiresCap: FsReadCap`

**`get_workflow_protocol`** — Input: `{}`. Output: the WORKFLOW board (branching, merge, and release rules). `requiresCap: FsReadCap`

**`get_em_swarm`** — Input: `{}`. Output: the STRUCTURE_EM board (E-M multi-agent topology). `requiresCap: FsReadCap`

**`get_milestone_status`** — Input: `{}`. Output: ROADMAP + SHIPPED merged (status and completed milestones). `requiresCap: FsReadCap`

**`audit_compact`** — Input: `{"keep_last_n":int}` (optional, default 100). Output: `{"dropped":<n>,"kept":<k>}` after dropping the oldest audit entries. `requiresCap: FsWriteCap`

### Capability Reference

The MCP server enforces a 14-bit capability token system. Each tool advertises its required cap as a bitmask in the `tools/list` response. A `requiresCap` of `0` means the default session cap is enough. Non-zero values mean the caller must hold those cap bits.

The 14 cap bits include filesystem read (`FsReadCap`), filesystem write (`FsWriteCap`), network bind (`BindCap`), and environment (`EnvCap`), among others. Read `ooda://orientation/capabilities` at runtime for the full table.

### Examples

Call a tool with no args (Tier 0, no cap):

```json
{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":3,"method":"tools/call","params":{"name":"get_orientation","arguments":{}}}
```

Call a tool with required args:

```json
{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":4,"method":"tools/call","params":{"name":"read_board","arguments":{"name":"NORTHSTAR"}}}
```

Call a tool with optional args:

```json
{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":5,"method":"tools/call","params":{"name":"get_audit_log","arguments":{"tail":50}}}
```

Unknown tool returns:

```json
{"error":"unknown tool: <name>"}
```

## PROTOCOL — Wire Protocol

The MCP server speaks JSON-RPC 2.0 over a Content-Length-framed stream transport (stdio, file, or Unix socket). The wire protocol is identical to LSP at the framing level, but the method namespace is MCP.

### 1. Framing

Each message is one HTTP-style header followed by a JSON body:

```
Content-Length: 87\r\n
\r\n
{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":1,"method":"initialize","params":{"protocolVersion":"2024-11-05"}}
```

The Content-Length is the byte count of the JSON body. The header is mandatory on stdio and socket; the file transport also accepts raw JSON without the header.

A single stream may carry multiple messages. The receiver reads bytes until the header is complete, then reads exactly `Content-Length` more bytes for the body.

### 2. Envelope

Standard JSON-RPC 2.0 envelope for every request, response, and notification.

Request:

```json
{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":1,"method":"<name>","params":{...}}
```

Response (success):

```json
{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":1,"result":<value>}
```

Response (error):

```json
{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":1,"error":{"code":-32601,"message":"Method not found: <name>"}}
```

Notification (no response expected):

```json
{"jsonrpc":"2.0","method":"<name>","params":{...}}
```

`id` may be a string or an integer. The server tracks seen `id` values to detect duplicates and rejects them with error `-32600`.

### 3. Standard error codes

| Code | Meaning |
|------|---------|
| `-32600` | Invalid request (empty method, duplicate id) |
| `-32601` | Method not found |
| `-32602` | Invalid params (schema mismatch, missing required arg) |
| `-32603` | Refused (cap revoked, session cancelled, URI outside roots) |
| `-32604` | Tier denies method |
| `-32605` | URI outside declared client roots |

## CLIENT_CONFIG — Client Configuration

This doc covers how to wire the openOODA MCP server into MCP-aware clients. The server is a stdio binary; the client spawns it, sends framed JSON-RPC over stdin, and reads framed JSON-RPC from stdout.

### 1. Launching the server directly

The server is a standalone binary. Run it under the ooda toolchain:

```sh
ooda mcp                # stdio (default)
ooda mcp --stdio        # explicit stdio
oooda mcp --file <path>  # one-shot file mode
oooda mcp --socket <path> # Unix socket
oooda mcp-merge <file>   # inject into a client config
```

For MCP clients, the typical entry point is `ooda mcp` (stdio). The client must keep the process alive for the duration of the session and route every JSON-RPC envelope through stdin and stdout.

### 2. Claude Desktop

Claude Desktop reads its MCP server list from a JSON config file. The config is at `claude_desktop_config.json` (the path varies by OS):

| OS | Path |
|----|------|
| macOS | `~/Library/Application Support/Claude/claude_desktop_config.json` |
| Linux | `~/.config/Claude/claude_desktop_config.json` |
| Windows | `%APPDATA%\Claude\claude_desktop_config.json` |

Add the openOODA server under `mcpServers`:

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "openooda": {
      "command": "ooda",
      "args": ["mcp"]
    }
  }
}
```

The `ooda` binary must be on the PATH visible to Claude Desktop. If it is not, give the absolute path:

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "openooda": {
      "command": "/home/user/.oodaup/bin/ooda",
      "args": ["mcp"]
    }
  }
}
```

Restart Claude Desktop after editing the config. The openOODA server should appear in the tool list with 23 tools.

### 3. Cursor

Cursor reads MCP server config from `~/.cursor/mcp.json` (or per-project `.cursor/mcp.json`):

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "openooda": {
      "command": "ooda",
      "args": ["mcp"]
    }
  }
}
```

Restart Cursor after editing the config.
